text:
[NDBG.2.4] **Services:** `ds_engine_service_count` / `_at` / `_find` return a
`ds_service_view_t` per service the loaded program declares, one per
`ServiceDef` atom (`proto/service_def.proto#ServiceDef`), with `_at` in the
artefact's order, which is source order ([RDSC.8.4]). `_at` must return `DS_ERR_NOT_FOUND` for an index past the
count. `_find` looks a service up by name and must report a miss through its
found flag with `DS_OK`, and leave the view unwritten, as
`ds_engine_rule_meta_find` does ([NDBG.2.3]).

The engine must give, for each service, every field below that the artefact
carries, and must keep each view's strings and kwarg array for the engine's
lifetime:

- the service's name;
- the response schema's name, empty for a service that declares `no response`
  ([LADP.8.4.2]), and a flag that is set exactly when it declares `no response`;
- its kwargs, in the artefact's order, which is by name ([LGRA.23.2]). Each
  gives its name; its declared type as the artefact spells it
  (`ServiceKwarg.ds_type`, [RDSC.6a.2.7]): a builtin type, a unit symbol, a
  dimension, a schema by its own name, the kind `Schema` or an opaque type, so the view carries the name and
  not a closed enumeration; whether it is `required` and whether it is
  `literal` ([LADP.8.5.1]); and its default, as the canonical text
  [RDSC.6a.2.4] gives, empty when it has none.

A service's hydration block is not in the view: hydration does not bind in
this edition.

This is how an integrator that hosts services learns what to assert for one:
a fact of the response schema with the call's correlation ([LCRS.4.3.1]), or
nothing for a `no response` service ([LADP.8.4.2]). It may also refuse to
register a callback under a name the loaded program does not declare. Reading
the `ServiceDef` atoms from the artefact's bytes instead would be a second
reader of what the engine loaded.

---
